records.source: וַֽיְהִי֙ הַמֶּ֣לֶךְ שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה מֶ֖לֶךְ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And was the king Solomon king over all Israel.
pieces: King Solomon ruled as king over all Israel.

L.1: And King Solomon was king over all Israel.

R.1: Solomon was now king over the whole nation of Israel.

decisions.choice: all Israel: the whole people, north and south together
decisions.reason: After the struggle for the throne in chapters 1-2 and the gift of wisdom in chapter 3, the writer states that Solomon's rule now reached the whole nation. The lists that follow show how that rule was organized: the officials of his court (verses 2-6) and the governors of the districts (verses 7-19).

decisions.choice: ruled as king (Balanced); was now king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "was king ... king". Balanced uses "ruled" to avoid the repetition. Readable adds "now" to mark the settled state after the events of chapters 1-3, and says "the whole nation" for "all Israel".

records.heading: Solomon's officials

records.source: וְאֵ֥לֶּה הַשָּׂרִ֖ים אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ עֲזַרְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־צָד֖וֹק הַכֹּהֵֽן׃ס
records.gloss: And these [were] the officials who [were] to him: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest.
pieces: These were his high officials: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest;

L.2: And these [were] the princes who [were] his: Azariah son of Zadok, the priest;

R.2: These were the leaders of Solomon's government: Azariah son of Zadok was the priest.

decisions.choice: the officials: the chief men of the king's court
decisions.reason: The word can name princes, commanders or officials. Here it introduces the men who held the main offices of Solomon's court, as similar lists do for David (2 Samuel 8:16-18; 20:23-26).

decisions.choice: son of Zadok: a descendant, probably his grandson
decisions.reason: The priestly line in 1 Chronicles 5:34-35 runs Zadok, Ahimaaz, Azariah, so this Azariah may be Zadok's grandson. "Son" in Hebrew can name any male descendant.

decisions.choice: the priest: Azariah's office
alternatives: Azariah, son of Zadok the priest
decisions.reason: In this list each name is followed by the man's office, so "the priest" most likely belongs to Azariah. It could also describe Zadok ("son of Zadok the priest"), who is named as a priest in verse 4.

decisions.choice: princes (Literal); high officials (Balanced); leaders of Solomon's government (Readable)
decisions.reason: This follows the usual wording for this word (Literal "princes", Balanced "officials", Readable "leaders"). Balanced adds "high" and Readable adds "of Solomon's government" because these are the king's chief ministers, not his sons.

decisions.choice: the list in verses 2-6 punctuated as one list
decisions.reason: The officials run on from verse 2 to verse 6, so Literal and Balanced end this verse with a semicolon. Readable uses full sentences.

records.source: אֱלִיחֹ֧רֶף וַאֲחִיָּ֛ה בְּנֵ֥י שִׁישָׁ֖א סֹפְרִ֑ים יְהוֹשָׁפָ֥ט בֶּן־אֲחִיל֖וּד הַמַּזְכִּֽיר׃
records.gloss: Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, [were] scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [was] the recorder.
pieces: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, served as secretaries; the recorder was Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud;

L.3: Elihoreph and Ahijah, sons of Shisha, [were] scribes; Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud [was] the recorder;

R.3: Elihoreph and Ahijah, the sons of Shisha, were the royal secretaries. Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the official records.

decisions.choice: secretaries and recorder: senior royal officials
decisions.reason: The secretary wrote the king's letters and records of state. The recorder (literally "one who causes to remember") kept the official records and may also have made the king's decisions known. Both offices appear among David's officials (2 Samuel 8:16-17) and Hezekiah's (Isaiah 36:3).

decisions.choice: Shisha: probably David's secretary under another form of his name
decisions.reason: David's secretary is called Seraiah (2 Samuel 8:17), Sheva (2 Samuel 20:25) and Shavsha (1 Chronicles 18:16). Shisha is very likely the same man, so his sons took over their father's office.

decisions.choice: Jehoshaphat son of Ahilud kept the post he had under David
decisions.reason: He was David's recorder too (2 Samuel 8:16; 20:24). Solomon kept some of his father's officials and replaced others (2:35).

decisions.choice: scribes (Literal); secretaries (Balanced, Readable); kept the official records (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew word for these officials means "one who writes", which Literal keeps as "scribes"; Balanced and Readable name the office. Readable says what the recorder did, as in Isaiah 36:3.

records.source: וּבְנָיָ֥הוּ בֶן־יְהוֹיָדָ֖ע עַל־הַצָּבָ֑א וְצָד֥וֹק וְאֶבְיָתָ֖ר כֹּהֲנִֽים׃ס
records.gloss: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada [was] over the army; and Zadok and Abiathar [were] priests.
pieces: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was commander of the army; Zadok and Abiathar were priests;

L.4: And Benaiah son of Jehoiada [was] over the army; and Zadok and Abiathar [were] priests;

R.4: Benaiah son of Jehoiada was the army commander. Zadok and Abiathar were priests.

decisions.choice: Benaiah over the army: Joab's replacement
decisions.reason: Solomon put Benaiah over the army in place of Joab after Joab was put to death (2:34-35).

decisions.choice: Abiathar: listed though Solomon had removed him
decisions.reason: Solomon had sent Abiathar away to Anathoth and put Zadok in his place (2:26-27, 35). His name here may come from the start of the reign, or he may have kept the title of priest after losing his place.

decisions.choice: commander of the army (Balanced); the army commander (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "over the army", which Literal keeps. Balanced and Readable use the usual title for this office in these books.

records.source: וַעֲזַרְיָ֥הוּ בֶן־נָתָ֖ן עַל־הַנִּצָּבִ֑ים וְזָב֧וּד בֶּן־נָתָ֛ן כֹּהֵ֖ן רֵעֶ֥ה הַמֶּֽלֶךְ׃
records.gloss: And Azariah son of Nathan [was] over the overseers; and Zabud son of Nathan [was] priest, friend of the king.
pieces: Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the district governors; Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's friend;

L.5: And Azariah son of Nathan [was] over the governors; and Zabud son of Nathan [was] a priest, [the] friend of the king;

R.5: Azariah son of Nathan was in charge of the governors of the districts. Zabud son of Nathan was a priest and the king's trusted adviser.

decisions.choice: the overseers: the twelve district governors
decisions.reason: The same word names the twelve men listed in verses 7-19, so Azariah was the official over all of them.

decisions.choice: friend of the king: a court office, the king's personal adviser
decisions.reason: "The king's friend" was a title. Hushai held it under David (2 Samuel 15:37; 16:16) and gave him counsel at a time of danger.

decisions.choice: priest: here perhaps a high official at the king's side
decisions.reason: The word normally means a priest. David's sons are also called priests (2 Samuel 8:18), where 1 Chronicles 18:17 says "first at the king's side", so here it may name a senior royal post rather than service at the altar.

decisions.choice: Nathan: probably one man, father of both officials
decisions.reason: This may be Nathan the prophet, who supported Solomon (1:11-14), or David's son Nathan (2 Samuel 5:14). The text does not say.

decisions.choice: district governors (Balanced, Readable); trusted adviser (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "district" to show these are the governors of verse 7. Readable explains the title "the king's friend".

records.source: וַאֲחִישָׁ֖ר עַל־הַבָּ֑יִת וַאֲדֹנִירָ֥ם בֶּן־עַבְדָּ֖א עַל־הַמַּֽס׃ס
records.gloss: And Ahishar [was] over the house; and Adoniram son of Abda [was] over the forced labor.
pieces: Ahishar was in charge of the palace, and Adoniram son of Abda had charge of the forced labor.

L.6: And Ahishar [was] over the house; and Adoniram son of Abda [was] over the forced labor.

R.6: Ahishar managed the king's palace. Adoniram son of Abda was in charge of the people who were forced to work for the king.

decisions.choice: over the house: chief steward of the royal palace
decisions.reason: The man "over the house" ran the king's household and estates and could speak for the king (Isaiah 22:15; 36:3; 2 Kings 15:5).

decisions.choice: the forced labor: work crews the king raised for his building
decisions.reason: The word names compulsory work for the state. Solomon's labor gangs built the temple, the palace and his fortified cities (5:27-28; 9:15-22). Adoniram, also called Adoram, held the post under David too (2 Samuel 20:24) and was still over it under Rehoboam (12:18); the burden of this labor helped split the kingdom (12:4, 18).

decisions.choice: in charge of the palace (Balanced); managed the king's palace; the people who were forced to work for the king (Readable)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says "over the house", which Literal keeps. Balanced uses the same wording as Isaiah 36:3. Readable explains what forced labor was.

records.source: וְלִשְׁלֹמֹ֞ה שְׁנֵים־עָשָׂ֤ר נִצָּבִים֙ עַל־כָּל־יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל וְכִלְכְּל֥וּ אֶת־הַמֶּ֖לֶךְ וְאֶת־בֵּית֑וֹ חֹ֧דֶשׁ בַּשָּׁנָ֛ה יִהְיֶ֥ה עַל־הָאֶחָ֖ד לְכַלְכֵּֽל׃ס
records.gloss: And to Solomon [were] twelve overseers over all Israel, and they supplied the king and his household; a month in the year was on the one to supply.
pieces: Solomon had twelve district governors over all Israel, who supplied food for the king and his household. Each of them had to provide for one month in the year.

L.7: And Solomon had twelve governors over all Israel, and they provided for the king and his household; a month in the year it was [laid] on each one to provide.

R.7: Solomon had twelve governors in charge of districts all over Israel. They supplied the food for the king and for everyone in his palace. Each governor had to provide the food for one month every year.

decisions.choice: supplied: provided food and goods for
decisions.reason: The verb means to sustain or feed, as Joseph fed his family in Egypt (Genesis 45:11; 47:12). The size of the daily supply is set out in 5:2-3 and 5:7-8.

decisions.choice: twelve districts: a new division of the land
decisions.reason: The districts in verses 8-19 do not simply follow the tribes. Some are named by tribe, others by towns and regions, so the old tribal lands were partly redrawn for the king's needs. Judah is not named in the list (see verse 19).

decisions.choice: each one: the written text and the traditional reading differ only by the word "the"
decisions.reason: The consonants written in the text and the reading handed down with it differ by the article on "one". Either way the sense is "each one".

decisions.choice: supplied food (Balanced, Readable); everyone in his palace (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what was supplied, as the following verses show. Readable explains "his household" as the people of the palace.

records.heading: Solomon's twelve district governors

records.source: וְאֵ֣לֶּה שְׁמוֹתָ֔ם בֶּן־ח֖וּר בְּהַ֥ר אֶפְרָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: And these [are] their names: Ben-hur, in [the] hill country of Ephraim.
pieces: These are their names: Ben-hur, in the hill country of Ephraim;

L.8: And these [are] their names: Ben-hur, in [the] hill country of Ephraim;

R.8: These are the names of the governors and their districts: Ben-hur (that is, the son of Hur) was over the hill country of Ephraim.

decisions.choice: Ben-hur: "son of Hur", a man known by his father's name
decisions.reason: Five of the governors are given only as "son of" someone (verses 8, 9, 10, 11 and 13). The list may come from a document whose first names were lost, or these men may simply have been known by their families. The name is kept as it stands.

decisions.choice: the hill country of Ephraim: the central highlands
decisions.reason: This was the heart of the northern tribes, around Shechem and Bethel.

decisions.choice: Ben-hur, Ben-deker, Ben-hesed, Ben-abinadab, Ben-geber at every level
decisions.reason: These five governors keep the Hebrew form as one name, joined with a hyphen, in all three levels. Readable explains the meaning once, here.

decisions.choice: the governors and their districts; was over
decisions.reason: Readable says what the list gives and supplies "was over" for each governor's district, here and in verses 9-19.

records.source: בֶּן־דֶּ֛קֶר בְּמָקַ֥ץ וּבְשַֽׁעַלְבִ֖ים וּבֵ֣ית שָׁ֑מֶשׁ וְאֵיל֖וֹן בֵּ֥ית חָנָֽן׃ס
records.gloss: Ben-deker, in Makaz and in Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan.
pieces: Ben-deker, in Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan;

L.9: Ben-deker, in Makaz and in Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan;

R.9: Ben-deker was over Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth-shemesh and Elon-beth-hanan.

decisions.choice: the western foothills, once the land of Dan
decisions.reason: Shaalbim and Beth-shemesh lie in the low hills west of Jerusalem, in the area first given to Dan (Joshua 19:41-43; Judges 1:35). Ben-deker is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: Elon-beth-hanan: one place
decisions.reason: The words may name one town, Elon-beth-hanan, or two, Elon and Beth-hanan. No town of either name is known for certain.

records.source: בֶּן־חֶ֖סֶד בָּֽאֲרֻבּ֑וֹת ל֥וֹ שֹׂכֹ֖ה וְכָל־אֶ֥רֶץ חֵֽפֶר׃ס
records.gloss: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; to him [were] Socoh and all [the] land of Hepher.
pieces: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; Socoh and all the land of Hepher were his;

L.10: Ben-hesed, in Arubboth; his [were] Socoh and all [the] land of Hepher;

R.10: Ben-hesed was over Arubboth. Socoh and the whole region of Hepher were also in his district.

decisions.choice: to him: belonging to his district
decisions.reason: "To him" means these places were under his charge, as in verse 13.

decisions.choice: Socoh and the land of Hepher: in the coastal plain of Sharon
decisions.reason: This Socoh is probably not the Socoh of Judah (Joshua 15:35) but a town in the plain north of it. Hepher was a clan area of Manasseh (Joshua 12:17; 17:2). Ben-hesed is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: the whole region of Hepher
decisions.reason: Readable says "region" for "land", since a part of the country is meant.

records.source: בֶּן־אֲבִֽינָדָ֖ב כָּל־נָ֣פַת דֹּ֑אר טָפַת֙ בַּת־שְׁלֹמֹ֔ה הָ֥יְתָה לּ֖וֹ לְאִשָּֽׁה׃ס
records.gloss: Ben-abinadab, all [the] height of Dor; Taphath daughter of Solomon became to him as wife.
pieces: Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor (Taphath, Solomon's daughter, was his wife);

L.11: Ben-abinadab, all Naphath-dor; Taphath daughter of Solomon became his wife;

R.11: Ben-abinadab was over all the hills around Dor. He was married to Taphath, Solomon's daughter.

decisions.choice: Naphath-dor: the heights of Dor
decisions.reason: Dor was a port on the coast south of Mount Carmel. The first word means "height" or "ridge", the hills behind the town (Joshua 11:2; 12:23). Ben-abinadab is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: Solomon's daughter as a governor's wife
decisions.reason: Marriage tied this governor, and Ahimaaz in verse 15, to the royal family and so to the king's interests.

decisions.choice: all the hills around Dor
decisions.reason: Readable explains the name Naphath-dor, as Joshua 11:2 does.

records.source: בַּֽעֲנָא֙ בֶּן־אֲחִיל֔וּד תַּעְנַ֖ךְ וּמְגִדּ֑וֹ וְכָל־בֵּ֣ית שְׁאָ֡ן אֲשֶׁר֩ אֵ֨צֶל צָרְתַ֜נָה מִתַּ֣חַת לְיִזְרְעֶ֗אל מִבֵּ֤ית שְׁאָן֙ עַ֚ד אָבֵ֣ל מְחוֹלָ֔ה עַ֖ד מֵעֵ֥בֶר לְיָקְמֳעָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: Baana son of Ahilud, Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean, which [is] beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as [the] other side of Jokmeam.
pieces: Baana son of Ahilud, in Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on beyond Jokmeam;

L.12: Baana son of Ahilud: Taanach and Megiddo and all Beth-shean, which [is] beside Zarethan below Jezreel, from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah, as far as beyond Jokmeam;

R.12: Baana son of Ahilud was over Taanach and Megiddo and the whole area of Beth-shean. That area lay next to Zarethan, below the town of Jezreel, and reached from Beth-shean to Abel-meholah and on past Jokmeam.

decisions.choice: the Jezreel valley and the Jordan valley near Beth-shean
decisions.reason: Taanach, Megiddo and Beth-shean were strong old cities that Manasseh could not take at first (Joshua 17:11; Judges 1:27). By Solomon's time they were part of the kingdom and formed one rich district across the great valley.

decisions.choice: which is beside Zarethan below Jezreel: a description of the Beth-shean area
decisions.reason: The clause tells where the district of Beth-shean lay: by Zarethan, in the Jordan valley, and lower than the town of Jezreel on the hills to the west. The next phrase gives its limits, south to Abel-meholah and beyond Jokmeam.

decisions.choice: Baana son of Ahilud: perhaps a brother of the recorder
decisions.reason: Jehoshaphat the recorder was also a son of Ahilud (verse 3). They may be brothers, but the text does not say.

decisions.choice: two sentences, with "that area"
decisions.reason: Readable divides the long description and repeats the subject, "that area", so the reader can follow where the district lay.

records.source: בֶּן־גֶּ֖בֶר בְּרָמֹ֣ת גִּלְעָ֑ד ל֡וֹ חַוֺּת֩ יָאִ֨יר בֶּן־מְנַשֶּׁ֜ה אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּגִּלְעָ֗ד ל֚וֹ חֶ֤בֶל אַרְגֹּב֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר בַּבָּשָׁ֔ן שִׁשִּׁים֙ עָרִ֣ים גְּדֹל֔וֹת חוֹמָ֖ה וּבְרִ֥יחַ נְחֹֽשֶׁת׃ס
records.gloss: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; to him [were the] villages of Jair son of Manasseh which [are] in Gilead; to him [was the] region of Argob which [is] in Bashan, sixty cities great, wall and bar[s] of bronze.
pieces: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead. The villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead were his, and so was the region of Argob in Bashan: sixty large cities with walls and bronze bars;

L.13: Ben-geber, in Ramoth-gilead; his [were] the villages of Jair son of Manasseh, which [are] in Gilead; his [was] the region of Argob, which [is] in Bashan, sixty great cities [with] wall[s] and bronze bar[s];

R.13: Ben-geber was over Ramoth-gilead. His district included the villages of Jair son of Manasseh in Gilead and the region of Argob in Bashan. There were sixty large cities there, with walls and with gates locked by bronze bars.

decisions.choice: the villages of Jair and the sixty cities of Argob: the lands taken under Moses
decisions.reason: Jair son of Manasseh took the region of Argob and named its villages after himself (Numbers 32:41; Deuteronomy 3:14). Deuteronomy 3:4-5 describes the sixty fortified cities of Argob with high walls, gates and bars.

decisions.choice: wall and bars of bronze: fortified towns
decisions.reason: The bars were the beams that held the city gates shut. Bronze made them harder to break or burn.

decisions.choice: Ramoth-gilead: a fortress town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: It was a city of refuge (Joshua 20:8) and later a battleground between Israel and Aram (22:3). Ben-geber is a "son of" name, as in verse 8.

decisions.choice: bronze bars (Balanced); gates locked by bronze bars (Readable)
decisions.reason: Readable says what the bars were for, as the note explains.

records.source: אֲחִֽינָדָ֥ב בֶּן־עִדֹּ֖א מַחֲנָֽיְמָה׃
records.gloss: Ahinadab son of Iddo, to Mahanaim.
pieces: Ahinadab son of Iddo, in Mahanaim;

L.14: Ahinadab son of Iddo, to Mahanaim;

R.14: Ahinadab son of Iddo was over Mahanaim.

decisions.choice: to Mahanaim: stationed at Mahanaim
decisions.reason: The place name has an ending that usually means "toward". Here it marks where the governor was placed, as "in" does for the others.

decisions.choice: Mahanaim: a town in Gilead, east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Jacob named it when he met God's angels there (Genesis 32:3). Ish-bosheth made it his capital, and David took refuge there from Absalom (2 Samuel 2:8; 17:24).

records.source: אֲחִימַ֖עַץ בְּנַפְתָּלִ֑י גַּם־ה֗וּא לָקַ֛ח אֶת־בָּשְׂמַ֥ת בַּת־שְׁלֹמֹ֖ה לְאִשָּֽׁה׃
records.gloss: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; also he took Basemath daughter of Solomon as wife.
pieces: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali (he too had married a daughter of Solomon, Basemath);

L.15: Ahimaaz, in Naphtali; he also took Basemath daughter of Solomon as [a] wife;

R.15: Ahimaaz was over Naphtali. He too had married one of Solomon's daughters, named Basemath.

decisions.choice: he also: like Ben-abinadab in verse 11
decisions.reason: "Also" links this marriage to Taphath's. Two governors were the king's sons-in-law.

decisions.choice: Ahimaaz: perhaps the son of Zadok
decisions.reason: Zadok's son Ahimaaz served David as a runner and messenger (2 Samuel 15:27, 36; 18:19). He may be this governor, but the name was not rare.

decisions.choice: Naphtali: the tribal land west of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: The district took the name of the tribe (Joshua 19:32-39).

decisions.choice: had married (Balanced, Readable)
decisions.reason: The marriage is background to the list, so Balanced and Readable use "had married", and Balanced sets it in parentheses as in verse 11.

records.source: בַּֽעֲנָא֙ בֶּן־חוּשָׁ֔י בְּאָשֵׁ֖ר וּבְעָלֽוֹת׃ס
records.gloss: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth.
pieces: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;

L.16: Baana son of Hushai, in Asher and Bealoth;

R.16: Baana son of Hushai was over Asher and Bealoth.

decisions.choice: Bealoth: a place in or near Asher
decisions.reason: No town of this name is known in the north. The same letters can be read "and in Aloth", another unknown place.

decisions.choice: Asher: the coastal land north of Mount Carmel; Hushai: perhaps David's friend
decisions.reason: Asher's land lay along the coast (Joshua 19:24-31). Baana's father may be Hushai the Archite, David's loyal adviser (2 Samuel 15:32-37), though the text does not say.

pieces: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;

L.17: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah, in Issachar;

R.17: Jehoshaphat son of Paruah was over Issachar.

decisions.choice: Issachar: the tribal land in and above the Jezreel valley
decisions.reason: The district took the tribe's name (Joshua 19:17-23). This Jehoshaphat is not the recorder of verse 3, who was a son of Ahilud.

pieces: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;

L.18: Shimei son of Ela, in Benjamin;

R.18: Shimei son of Ela was over Benjamin.

decisions.choice: Shimei son of Ela: not the Shimei of chapter 2
decisions.reason: Shimei son of Gera, who cursed David, had been put to death (2:46). This governor may be the Shimei who stood with Solomon in 1:8. Benjamin was the tribe just north of Jerusalem.

records.gloss: Geber son of Uri, in [the] land of Gilead, [the] land of Sihon king of the Amorite and Og king of Bashan; and governor one who [was] in the land.
pieces: Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the territory of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan. In the land there was one governor.

L.19: Geber son of Uri, in the land of Gilead, the land of Sihon king of the Amorites and of Og king of Bashan; and one governor who [was] in the land.

R.19: Geber son of Uri was over the land of Gilead. Long before, this land had belonged to Sihon king of the Amorites and to Og king of Bashan. In the land there was one governor.

decisions.choice: the land of Sihon and Og: the kingdoms east of the Jordan taken under Moses
decisions.reason: Israel defeated Sihon and Og and gave their land to Reuben, Gad and half of Manasseh (Numbers 21:21-35; Deuteronomy 3:1-17). Ben-geber's district (verse 13) lay in Gilead too, so these two districts shared the land east of the Jordan.

decisions.choice: one governor who was in the land: meaning unclear
alternatives: he was the only governor in that land
and one governor over the land of Judah
decisions.reason: The words may mean that Geber was the only governor over this wide region, or that there was one more governor, over "the land", perhaps Judah, which the list does not otherwise name. The ancient Greek translation has "in the land of Judah" here. The Hebrew can bear both readings, and all levels keep it open.

decisions.choice: Long before, this land had belonged to
decisions.reason: Readable explains that the names of Sihon and Og recall who once ruled the land.

records.source: יְהוּדָ֤ה וְיִשְׂרָאֵל֙ רַבִּ֔ים כַּח֥וֹל אֲשֶׁר־עַל־הַיָּ֖ם לָרֹ֑ב אֹכְלִ֥ים וְשֹׁתִ֖ים וּשְׂמֵחִֽים׃
records.gloss: Judah and Israel [were] many like the sand which [is] by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing.
pieces: Judah and Israel were as many as the sand by the sea; they ate and drank and were glad.

L.20: Judah and Israel [were] many, like the sand that [is] by the sea in multitude, eating and drinking and rejoicing.

R.20: The people of Judah and Israel were as many as the grains of sand on the seashore. They had plenty to eat and drink, and they were happy.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text ends chapter 4 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 4 ends at this verse, and the next fourteen verses (Solomon's wide rule, his daily provisions and his wisdom) begin chapter 5 as 5:1-14. Many Bibles number them 4:21-34, and so number the rest of chapter 5 (5:15-32 here) 5:1-18. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: as many as the sand by the sea: God's promise to Abraham kept
decisions.reason: God promised Abraham to make his offspring like the sand on the seashore (Genesis 22:17; see also 32:13). The writer shows that promise fulfilled in Solomon's day.

decisions.choice: eating and drinking and rejoicing: peace and plenty
decisions.reason: The three words picture a people with enough food, at peace and glad, under a king who ruled them well. "Judah and Israel" names the south and the north together, still one kingdom.

decisions.choice: grains of sand; had plenty to eat and drink
decisions.reason: Readable says "grains" so the comparison is about number, and puts the picture of eating and drinking as having plenty.
